the induced electric current in the body of the MRI worker is influenced by motion speed and the intensity of the static magnetic field of the MRI scanner, and that the induced current is more influenced by the intensity of the field than the motion speed of the MRI operator.

the induced electric current density is influenced by the motion speed in static field of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanners.

the influence of motion speed in MRI scanners on the induced electric current in the bodies of operators, and it was concluded that the magnet intensity was a more influential factor than the operator's motion speed on induced current values.
a new and unexplored field of MRI safety, namely, the influence of motion speed on induced electric currents in MRI workers.

, the ICNIRPs recommended guidelines for occupational exposures are not exceeded in the present study.
the ICNIRPMRI guidelines should be revised to take into account the influence of the operator motion speed in the induced electric currents in MRI workers.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the presence of static magnetic fields, the intensity of induced electric currents is influenced by both, the magnetic flux densities and the speed of motion of operators.
, the induced electric current density values are not influenced by motion speed but are influenced by magnetic flux density.
the intensity of induced currents is a function of the magnetic field strength and motion speed of MRI operators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, it is important for MRI operators to be well informed about the potential risks of exposure to the magnetic fields of MRI machines.
, it is the magnetic field intensity that is the most influencing factor in the induced current in bodies of MRI personnel and not their motion speed as has been thought.
, MRI scanners with higher magnetic flux density and faster motion speed by operators, will result in higher induced electric currents in MRI operators.
